provisional_options.name: Lean full-snapshot-per-request helper with constant certificate
provisional_options.assessment: Primary simplicity candidate for independent review, not an approved design. Freshly collect and validate every required history/input on each request, using one exact immutable byte view per file for both semantic checks and hashes; never reuse a history cache across requests. A private trusted helper can return bounded job nonce/request digest/supervisor version/validated binding and success/failure rather than every historical path/hash row. Parent must reject stale internal version and mismatched correlated identity; a blanket verification bypass is forbidden. Source validation uses the actual declared commit/working bytes and parsed templates from that same view.
provisional_options.linearization_limit: Name each guard observation and its captured bytes. A request can observe a counter during its execution and a later external change need not imply a global multi-file transaction violation. However no single simultaneous all-input point has been proved for independently captured mutable files, and no last-publication currentness claim follows. Required current-attempt/reconciliation semantics and acceptable concurrent-write ordering must be resolved by independent review against exact original clauses before code.
provisional_options.deadline_limit: Full-history I/O runs outside the supervisor and emits constant-size transport, while the supervisor services runtime/control/deadline traffic. That removes frame growth and event-loop blocking; it does not prove arbitrary histories complete inside a fixed control deadline. Helper deadline failure must be truthful, stop/clean only proven owned groups, retain uncertainty and never fabricate cancellation. Existing observed cancellation deadlines continue independently. Worst-case valid-history safety-call availability remains unmeasured and must be resolved rather than silently weakened.

provisional_options.name: Read leases for bytes plus namespace monitoring for names
provisional_options.assessment: Not disproved by either isolated primitive test. Read leases can reject existing writable mappings and prevent conflicting new writer access, while a separately complete namespace observer could detect replacement/rename. Must acquire leases before reading, cover all actual authoritative regular inputs and namespace ancestors, bind exact bytes, retain lease FDs through handoff/helper cleanup and inspect lease-break state. SIGIO or a nominal 45-second host timer cannot be assumed to provide complete authority.
provisional_options.linearization_hypothesis: A possible observation proof uses a monotone no-reacquire lease interval and an event-free namespace epoch: all input leases acquired before validation, subsequently verified still read-held, with namespace monitoring spanning capture through final drain. Exact common observation point and lease-break ordering require independent proof; no currentness-through-publication claim is established.
provisional_options.unproven: No complete combined observer, signal/forced-break race qualification, SCM_RIGHTS lease transfer, helper-death lease ownership, monitor overflow/setup/ancestor coverage, Git reference/object/backend enumeration, descriptor-budget scaling or cancellation bound was exercised. Source3 source_provenance invokes multiple Git commands; replacing HEAD with a pinned revision alone does not prove live HEAD checks. Directory lease failure alone is not a reason to reject the combined family.

provisional_options.name: Sealed immutable transaction inputs
provisional_options.assessment: Full memfd seals can enforce unchanged copied bytes across FD transfer and helper death, unlike F_SEAL_FUTURE_WRITE. This can transport exact validated snapshots, but it does not freeze original authoritative paths or prove their currentness. Treating a copied transaction as new authority, changing counter ownership, moving mutable durable state to a new service, requiring cooperative writers or changing public request semantics would require explicit proposed contract/authority review. No such change is made or automatically recommended here.

sources.used_for: Leases attach to open file descriptions and only regular files; duplicate FDs share lifetime. Conflicting writable opens/truncation trigger a break and can proceed after forced timer expiry. During a pending break F_GETLEASE reports the target lease type. Ownership/filesystem restrictions must fail closed.

Full write sealing fails with a preexisting writable shared mapping; after sealing kernel rejects writes/new shared writable maps. Future-write-only sealing leaves existing writable mappings effective. Seals persist with underlying file rather than helper lifetime.
Replacing a pathname is atomic for that pathname; existing open descriptions and other hardlinks remain associated with their original object.
Ordinary local flock is advisory; it is not sufficient exclusion against an uncooperative existing mapper/writer. No flock substitute is proposed.
